title: Spiced Hibiscus Iced Tea with Orange and Ginger
changes_from_base: Black tea replaced by a caffeine-free hibiscus infusion steeped with citrus zest, ginger and whole spices and sweetened with honey.
summary: A deep ruby, caffeine-free iced tea: dried hibiscus steeped with citrus peel, ginger and whole spices, sweetened with honey and served very cold.

ingredients.item: orange: 4 wide strips of zest and 30 ml juice
lemon: 4 wide strips of zest and 30 ml juice

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Bring the water to the boil in a large saucepan, then take the pan off the heat.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Add the hibiscus, the orange and lemon zest strips and juices, the ginger, cinnamon, star anise and cloves. Cover and leave for 20 minutes; the liquid turns ruby and smells warmly spiced. Steeping off the heat keeps the flavour bright rather than stewed.

steps.title: Strain and sweeten
steps.text: Pour through a fine sieve into a large jug, pressing the flowers lightly, and stir in the honey while the liquid is still warm so it dissolves completely.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Let it cool, then refrigerate for at least an hour. Taste again once cold, since chilling dulls sweetness, and add more honey if needed.

tips: Leaving the flowers in for much longer than 20 minutes makes the tea astringent; strain on time.
Use a vegetable peeler for the zest and avoid the white pith, which is bitter.
Hibiscus stains wooden spoons and pale worktops; wipe spills quickly.
storage: Keeps up to 7 days in a covered jug in the fridge. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
